question: Using determinants, obtain the equation of the line joining $(a,0)$ and $(0,b)$, where $a\ne0$ and $b\ne0$. Hence, express it in intercept form.
explanation:
Collinearity determinant
Let $(x,y)$ be any point on the line joining $(a,0)$ and $(0,b)$. The three points satisfy $$\begin{vmatrix}x&y&1\\a&0&1\\0&b&1\end{vmatrix}=0$$
Expansion of the determinant
Expanding along the first row, $$x(0-b)-y(a-0)+ab=0$$
Equation in standard form
This simplifies to $$bx+ay=ab$$
Conversion to intercept form
Since $a\ne0$ and $b\ne0$, divide throughout by $ab$: $$\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1$$
Hence, the intercepts of the line on the coordinate axes are $a$ and $b$.
